name: Niamey
subtitle: Niamey, capital of Niger: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: Niamey numbered 1,026,848 residents across five municipal arrondissements in the 2012 census.
Capital of Niger since 1926 when the French colonial administration relocated headquarters from Zinder to the banks of the Niger River.
The 24-hectare Musée National Boubou Hama and Grand Marché form celebrated epicenters of Sahelian cultural heritage and trade.

parts.text: Originating as a peaceful Zarma fishing and farming village on the eastern banks of the majestic Niger River, Niamey developed into a vital administrative and trade crossroads connecting the Sahel and West African coasts.
In 1926, the French colonial administration transferred the territorial capital of the Colony of Niger from Zinder to Niamey, spurring the construction of civic infrastructure along the riverbanks.

Following full national independence in August 1960 under President Hamani Diori, Niamey expanded into a vibrant metropolis celebrated for its open-air museum, universities, and bustling riverfront commerce.

blocks.prompt: About how many people lived in Niamey in the 2012 census?

parts.text: 1,026,848 inhabitants recorded in the December 2012 census by the Institut National de la Statistique du Niger across five arrondissements.

items.text: French forces establish a colonial military garrison at Niamey along the Niger River.
Niamey officially replaces Zinder as the territorial capital of the Colony of Niger.
Establishment of the Musée National du Niger (later Musée National Boubou Hama).
Niger proclaims full independence on 3 August 1960 with Niamey as sovereign capital.
